subject: Clarification: Data export controls, DPF evidence and DPA annex for Lakeshore Health
messages:
From: Maria Ortega <compliance@lakeshorehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@lakeshorehealth.com>, procurement@lakeshorehealth.com
Date: Thu, 09 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: RFI: Data export controls / DPF evidence request

Karthik,

Thanks for taking this RFI. Lakeshore is compiling evidence to support our vendor risk assessment. We reviewed the initial materials but need clarifications on several cross-border and data protection topics before we progress to legal review. Can you confirm the following (we've attached our questionnaire v1):

1) Data flows & jurisdictions: For hosted (Redwood API) vs Dedicated vs Private deployments, can you provide a concise mapping of where customer content, logs, and model artifacts reside (region-level) and which transfers rely on EU->US or APAC routing?

2) DPF / SCCs: Do you rely on EU SCCs, the EU-US DPF (if and when accepted), or another transfer mechanism? If SCCs, which module(s) and what controls complement them (e.g., encryption at rest + processing agreements)?

3) Subprocessors & chaining: Full list of subprocessors (infra, telemetry, logging). How do you notify customers of changes and offer export controls for Private deployments?

4) Key management & HSM: Can keys be customer-managed in KMS/HSM in Private and Dedicated? For hosted, what's the default key custody model?

5) Operational evidence: sample audit log schema, retention windows, how long KV caches and prefix caches persist, and whether we can request deletion of logs or traces per-route.

6) Ability to avoid model training: confirm that customer-provided data will never be used to train public models; and for hosted tiers, whether telemetry is used to improve model quality.

7) Latency & routing: for EU customers, typical e2e latency figures (p50/p95) for small chat requests on hosted vs Dedicated; any scenario where traffic is routed through non-EU regions.

We'd like the answers in line-item format and any supporting artifacts (network diagram, DPA annex redline, mapping CSV). Can we target a follow-up call week of Nov 20?

Thanks,
Maria Ortega
Head of Privacy & Risk
Lakeshore Health

Attachment: lakeshore_questionnaire_v1.xlsx
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maria Ortega <compliance@lakeshorehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Nov 2028 11:07:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RFI: Data export controls / DPF evidence request

Maria —

Appreciate the clear list. Below are concise responses; I've attached a short evidence pack (CSV + network topology + proposed DPA annex). I'll also add a mapping spreadsheet that ties your questionnaire rows to specific evidence artifacts. If you want, we can schedule a technical workshop on Nov 20 (I have 10–12 ET open).

1) Data flows & jurisdictions:
- Hosted (Redwood API): customer content and transient inference state are processed in the requested region when available. Persistent telemetry and aggregated anonymized usage metrics are stored in our primary analytics region (US-East) by default; customers can request EU-only retention via Redwood Private or Dedicated with region pinning.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools deployed in a chosen cloud region; logs and state are stored in that region by default; optional cross-region backups are asynchronous and customers can opt-out.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control plane within your VPC; no cross-border flow unless you explicitly enable vendor-managed backups.

2) DPF / SCCs:
- We implement EU SCCs for processor->subprocessor relationships. For EU->US transfers we currently support the EU-US DPF mapping where customers require it (evidence attached). We can also operate under SCCs and provide a DPA annex that includes the technical and organizational measures referenced in the SCCs.

3) Subprocessors & chaining:
- Current subprocessors listed in attached CSV (infra: major cloud compute + object storage; telemetry: third-party metrics provider; logging: internal ELK-managed service hosted by our infra provider).
- Notification: 30-day notice for additions; emergency changes notified within 72 hours with mitigation options.

4) Key management & HSM:
- Private: support for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS, support for HSM-backed keys).
- Dedicated: option for customer KMS in the region; standard offering is Redwood-managed KMS.
- Hosted: default is Redwood-managed KMS; we offer customer-managed keys under an enterprise add-on.

5) Operational evidence:
- Audit logs: event-level schema attached (audit_log_schema.csv). Default retention: 90 days for request/response logs; 365 days for billing/usage records.
- KV/prefix caches: in-memory by default; cache TTL configurable per-route (default 5 minutes for prefix caches; session KV caches ephemeral to session lifetime).
- Deletion: we can action deletion requests for logs and stored traces; documented SLA for deletions is 30 days from request in hosted, 7 days in Dedicated/Private (customer-administered).

6) Model training / telemetry:
- Customer content is not used to train our public models. For hosted tiers, telemetry that could improve model quality is limited and anonymized; opt-out available at account level. Private deployments have no telemetry to Redwood unless explicitly enabled.

7) Latency & routing:
- Typical p50/p95 (short chat request, 64-token): Hosted EU region: p50 ~45ms, p95 ~120ms. Dedicated EU region: p50 ~30ms, p95 ~75ms (depends on model size and instance type). Traffic for EU customers is routed within EU when EU region selected; fallbacks to non-EU occur only during region-wide outages and are governed by customer routing policy in the Console.

Attached: redwood_dpf_mapping_lakeshore.csv, dpa-annex-proposed.docx, network-topology-private-deploy.pdf, audit_log_schema.csv.

Next steps: please confirm a Nov 20 slot for the workshop and any additional rows you want us to expand into evidence.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpf_mapping_lakeshore.csv; dpa-annex-proposed.docx; network-topology-private-deploy.pdf; audit_log_schema.csv
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Nov 2028 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Fw: RFI: Data export controls / DPF evidence request

Karthik / Marissa —

Quick internal note before we send the final evidence bundle: Laura (legal) suggestions —
- Reduce default audit log retention in the DPA annex to 30 days for request/response logs with an option for customers to extend to 90 days (sales will need to flag revenue/ops tradeoffs).
- Add explicit language that Redwood will not use customer content for model training unless a separate training agreement is executed.
- Provide a subprocessors table with contact roles and subprocess descriptions (we can pull from the CSV).

Marissa — can you validate the HSM wording in section 4 and confirm the exact SLA for deletion (we stated 30 days for hosted; legal prefers 45 unless engineering confirms 30)?

Thanks — let me know if you want me to redline dpa-annex-proposed.docx before we send.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks for the thorough responses and the attachments. A couple of quick follow-ups from our side after an initial review:

• Can you provide a short sample of the audit log (sanitized) and a CSV that maps our questionnaire row IDs to the evidence files you attached? That will help expedite legal review.
• Regarding retention: Lakeshore prefers 30 days for request/response logs but requires an option to extend to 90 for forensics. Could you reflect that in the annex as a configurable default with opt-in extension?
• For DPF/SCCs: please confirm if you will accept execution of our redlined DPA annex and whether the DocuSign flow is acceptable.

We are targeting a technical workshop Nov 20 11:00 ET — does that work for your team? Evan and I will be on the call; procurement may join to discuss timelines.

Best,
Maria Ortega
Head of Privacy & Risk
Lakeshore Health
